name: Account Opening Procedure
description: End-to-end procedure for opening customer accounts at FirstUK Bank, encompassing identity verification, compliance checks, and account activation. Applies across branch, digital onboarding, and operations channels. Effective from 2026-03-01 with review scheduled for 2027-03-01.
context: FirstUK Bank — Account Opening Procedure
Document ID | ACCT-OPEN-SOP-001
Effective Date | 2026-03-01
Audience | Branch, Digital Onboarding, Operations, Compliance

name: Head of Retail Banking
description: Senior leadership role responsible for ownership and governance of the Account Opening Procedure at FirstUK Bank.
context: Owner | Head of Retail Banking

name: Customer Identity and Address Verification
description: Know Your Customer compliance obligation referenced as a related procedure within the account opening workflow. Detailed in separate SOP document for verification methodology and documentation requirements.
context: Related Documents | [[policy_customer_identification_v2]], [[policy_aml]], [[sop_kyc_verification]]

name: Anti-Money Laundering Screening
description: AML compliance control integrated into the account opening procedure, referenced through related policy documentation. Ensures customer screening against sanctions and PEP lists prior to account activation.
context: Related Documents | [[policy_customer_identification_v2]], [[policy_aml]], [[sop_kyc_verification]]

name: Individual Customer
description: Natural person applying for or opening an account through the FirstUK Bank Account Opening Procedure. Subject to identity verification, compliance screening, and account holder obligations.
context: Audience | Branch, Digital Onboarding, Operations, Compliance

name: New Account
description: Banking account established through the Account Opening Procedure at FirstUK Bank. Subject to KYC verification, AML screening, and compliance checkpoints before activation.
context: FirstUK Bank — Account Opening Procedure

name: Customer Identification Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate requiring verification of customer identity and screening against sanctions/PEP lists before account opening can proceed. Governed by policy_customer_identification_v2.
context: Related Documents | [[policy_customer_identification_v2]], [[policy_aml]], [[sop_kyc_verification]]

name: AML Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate ensuring anti-money laundering screening is completed and passed before account activation. Governed by policy_aml and integrated into the account opening workflow.
context: Related Documents | [[policy_customer_identification_v2]], [[policy_aml]], [[sop_kyc_verification]]

name: Enhanced KYC Implementation Procedure
description: A comprehensive Know Your Customer procedure implementing enhanced KYC requirements effective from 2026-03-01. This procedure supersedes the previous Version 2.1 in full, establishing new identity and address verification standards for customer onboarding and ongoing compliance.
context: Implement enhanced-KYC requirements from 2026-03-01
This procedure supersedes Version 2.1 in full from that date

name: Enhanced KYC Verification
description: Enhanced Know Your Customer verification requirements mandated from 2026-03-01 onwards. This represents an upgrade from the previous KYC standard (Version 2.1) with strengthened identity and address verification controls.
context: Implement enhanced-KYC requirements from 2026-03-01
This procedure supersedes Version 2.1 in full from that date

name: Risk Classification Before Account Activation
description: An end-to-end procedure that classifies customer risk before account activation. The process identifies applicant type, applies standard risk assessment, flags high-risk customers for enhanced due diligence, and enforces approval gates before credential issuance or deposit acceptance.
context: Risk Classify Before Activation
Identify whether the applicant is an individual or entity
Apply the standard customer-risk assessment
Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`
Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: Applicant Type Identification
description: The first step in risk classification where the responsible actor determines whether the applicant is an individual or an entity. This classification determines which risk assessment rules apply.
context: Identify whether the applicant is an individual or entity

name: Standard Customer Risk Assessment
description: The step where standard customer-risk assessment criteria are applied to the applicant based on their identified type. This assessment determines the customer's risk classification.
context: Apply the standard customer-risk assessment

name: High-Risk Customer Flagging
description: The step where customers identified as high-risk are marked as 'Pending Enhanced Due Diligence'. This flag prevents account activation until enhanced due diligence is completed and approved.
context: Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`

name: Approval Gate Verification Before Activation
description: The final step that enforces approval gates before credentials are issued or initial deposits are accepted. This step ensures all compliance and risk checks have passed before account activation.
context: Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: High-Risk Customer Gate
description: A branching decision point where the customer's risk assessment outcome determines whether they proceed to standard activation or are flagged for enhanced due diligence. High-risk customers are held pending approval; standard-risk customers proceed.
context: Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`
Apply the standard customer-risk assessment

name: Approval Gates Pass Decision
description: A gate decision that determines whether all approval conditions have been satisfied before credentials are issued and deposits are accepted. Failure to pass gates blocks account activation.
context: Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: Risk Classification Assessor
description: The role responsible for identifying applicant type, applying standard risk assessment, and marking high-risk customers for enhanced due diligence during the pre-activation risk classification process.
context: Identify whether the applicant is an individual or entity
Apply the standard customer-risk assessment
Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`

name: Approval Gate Authority
description: The role responsible for verifying that all approval gates have passed before credentials are issued or initial deposits are accepted. This role enforces the activation authorization decision.
context: Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate that verifies enhanced due diligence requirements have been satisfied for high-risk customers before account activation is permitted. This checkpoint ensures regulatory risk management obligations are met.
context: Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`
Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: Applicant
description: The natural person or entity applying for an account who is subject to risk classification before activation. The applicant's type (individual or entity) and risk profile determine the activation pathway.
context: Identify whether the applicant is an individual or entity
Apply the standard customer-risk assessment
Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`

name: High-Risk Customer
description: A customer identified through standard risk assessment as presenting elevated compliance or financial crime risk. High-risk customers are flagged as 'Pending Enhanced Due Diligence' and cannot proceed to account activation until enhanced due diligence is completed and approved.
context: Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`
Do not issue credentials or accept an initial deposit until approval gates pass

name: Standard Customer Risk Assessment
description: The KYC-related risk assessment process applied to all applicants to determine their risk classification. This assessment is a prerequisite to account activation and determines whether enhanced due diligence is required.
context: Apply the standard customer-risk assessment
Mark a high-risk customer as `Pending Enhanced Due Diligence`

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Gate
description: A mandatory compliance checkpoint within account onboarding that verifies beneficial ownership, source of funds, and sanctions/PEP screening before account approval. The gate requires documented evidence collection and formal compliance sign-off.
context: Step 2: Enhanced Due Diligence Gate
Beneficial owners | Identity and ownership/control evidence for every owner above 25%
Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results
Approval | Compliance approval and any documented exception decision

name: Beneficial Owner Verification
description: Verification that identity and ownership/control evidence is collected and recorded for every beneficial owner holding above 25% stake in the account holder entity.
context: Beneficial owners | Identity and ownership/control evidence for every owner above 25%

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: Verification that credible evidence of legitimate source of funds is obtained and recorded for any initial deposit exceeding £10,000.
context: Source of funds | Credible evidence for an initial deposit above £10,000

name: Enhanced Sanctions and PEP Screening
description: Mandatory screening against multiple sanctions and PEP databases including OFAC, EU, UN, HMT lists, with adverse media checks, to identify politically exposed persons and sanctioned entities before account approval.
context: Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results

name: Compliance Approval Gate
description: Final formal approval by Compliance leadership (Head of Compliance or CRO) to proceed with account opening, including documented exception decisions where applicable.
context: Approval | Compliance approval and any documented exception decision

name: Onboarding Analyst
description: Operations role responsible for collecting and recording beneficial owner identity evidence and source of funds documentation during the Enhanced Due Diligence Gate.
context: Beneficial owners | Identity and ownership/control evidence for every owner above 25% | Onboarding Analyst
Source of funds | Credible evidence for an initial deposit above £10,000 | Onboarding Analyst

name: Financial Crime Analyst
description: Specialist role responsible for executing enhanced screening checks against OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, and adverse media databases during the Enhanced Due Diligence Gate.
context: Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results | Financial Crime Analyst

name: Head of Compliance / CRO
description: Senior compliance authority responsible for final approval of account opening following Enhanced Due Diligence Gate completion, with authority to document and approve exceptions.
context: Approval | Compliance approval and any documented exception decision | Head of Compliance / CRO

name: OFAC Screening
description: Screening against the Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions list as part of enhanced due diligence during account onboarding.
context: Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results

name: PEP Screening
description: Screening to identify politically exposed persons as part of enhanced due diligence during account onboarding.
context: Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results

name: Adverse Media Check
description: Screening for adverse media coverage as part of enhanced due diligence during account onboarding.
context: Enhanced screening | OFAC, EU, UN, HMT, PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media results

name: Approval and Activation
description: Final approval gate for account activation following KYC assessment. Routes to Head of Compliance for standard approval, CRO for policy exceptions, or Financial Crime for high-risk matches. Establishes next review date upon approval.
context: No material concern: Head of Compliance approves activation.
Policy exception requested: document the rationale and obtain CRO approval.
Positive match, suspicious funds, or unclear ownership: refer to Financial Crime; do not activate or tip off the customer.
After approval, set the next review three months from activation and store the review date in the KYC record.

name: Material Concern Assessment
description: Branching decision determining whether KYC assessment presents material compliance concerns. Routes to standard approval, exception handling, or Financial Crime escalation based on risk outcome.
context: No material concern: Head of Compliance approves activation.
Policy exception requested: document the rationale and obtain CRO approval.
Positive match, suspicious funds, or unclear ownership: refer to Financial Crime

name: Policy Exception Trigger
description: Decision point identifying when a policy exception is required during approval. Triggers documentation of rationale and escalation to CRO for authority.
context: Policy exception requested: document the rationale and obtain CRO approval.

name: High-Risk Match or Suspicious Activity Detection
description: Detection gate for positive sanctions/PEP matches, suspicious funds indicators, or unclear beneficial ownership. Triggers mandatory Financial Crime referral and account non-activation.
context: Positive match, suspicious funds, or unclear ownership: refer to Financial Crime; do not activate or tip off the customer.

name: Head of Compliance
description: Authority responsible for approving account activation when no material compliance concerns are identified during KYC assessment.
context: No material concern: Head of Compliance approves activation.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Senior authority required to approve policy exceptions during the KYC approval process when standard compliance rules require deviation.
context: Policy exception requested: document the rationale and obtain CRO approval.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Specialist team responsible for investigating and handling high-risk matches, suspicious funds indicators, and unclear ownership scenarios. Determines whether account activation proceeds.
context: Positive match, suspicious funds, or unclear ownership: refer to Financial Crime; do not activate or tip off the customer.

name: KYC Approval Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate verifying that KYC assessment is complete and risk classification determined before account activation is permitted. Requires documented approval outcome.
context: No material concern: Head of Compliance approves activation.
Policy exception requested: document the rationale and obtain CRO approval.
Positive match, suspicious funds, or unclear ownership: refer to Financial Crime

name: KYC Record
description: Customer KYC documentation and verification record maintained throughout the account lifecycle. Stores identity, address, and risk assessment data, with next review date set at activation and updated periodically.
context: After approval, set the next review three months from activation and store the review date in the KYC record.

name: Quality Control and Exceptions Procedure
description: A procedure for managing quality control reviews and exception handling in file processing. High-risk files undergo secondary review, and missing documents trigger escalation rather than being treated as minor exceptions. Policy conflicts are resolved by applying the current customer identification policy.
context: A second reviewer checks high-risk files.
A missing document is not a minor exception: resolve it or escalate under `[[sop_exception_handling]]`.
Apply `[[policy_customer_identification_v2]]` if policy and training material differ.

name: High-Risk File Secondary Review
description: A second reviewer conducts quality control checks on high-risk files as part of the exception handling procedure.
context: A second reviewer checks high-risk files.

name: Missing Document Resolution or Escalation
description: When a document is missing from a file, the exception must be resolved or escalated according to the exception handling SOP rather than being treated as a minor issue.
context: A missing document is not a minor exception: resolve it or escalate under `[[sop_exception_handling]]`.

name: Policy Conflict Resolution
description: When policy documentation and training materials conflict, the current customer identification policy version 2 is applied to resolve the discrepancy.
context: Apply `[[policy_customer_identification_v2]]` if policy and training material differ.

name: Second Reviewer
description: An operations staff member responsible for conducting secondary quality control reviews on high-risk files to ensure compliance and accuracy.
context: A second reviewer checks high-risk files.

name: Customer Identification Verification
description: A compliance checkpoint requiring verification of customer identification documentation. The current policy version (v2) governs the standards and procedures for this verification when conflicts arise between policy and training materials.
context: Apply `[[policy_customer_identification_v2]]` if policy and training material differ.
